gaps.issue: I ran a fresh probe of 36 single-line mutants that the builder had not listed. 24 survived the full 40-test suite. Four of the survivors change published output with no test failing. (1) Replacing the per-fund floor max() in calculate() with the issuer floor moves the BUIDL floor from $975.38m to $548.53m and the USYC floor from $2.376bn to $2.300bn. That moves the basket floor from $4.907bn to $4.405bn, unresolved coverage at the floor from $1.351bn to $0.848bn and slack from $4.272bn to $4.774bn. All three are published in RESULTS, as is the 1.77% floor ratio. The only test asserts an identity that the mutant preserves. (2) Valuing OUSG exclusions at the high NAV instead of the low NAV moves the direct upper bound from 0.62199688 to 0.62199352, but the test only checks 0.6219 < upper < 0.6220. (3) Removing the max(ZERO, ...) clamp makes the custody-inclusive shortfall -$160.41m. (4) Setting the BENJI exclusion mark to $1 changes balances, but only by an amount near rounding. The other 20 survivors are input guards that no corrupted-copy case trips. In load_evidence: the read's block parameter, the successor block number and block timestamp, the Curve coin-address match, the Frax deposit destination match, the RPC cutoff field, USYC NAV > 0, and the Franklin filing's report period, class and B.5 share count. In ousg_model: the OUSG mark timestamp set. In gated_receipt: the underlying-identity check. In calculate(): duplicate fund, floor/ceiling order, nonpositive position and unknown kind. In the STBL credit: the net-deposit cap, which does not bind on this data. In check_post_card: the PNG header and size checks and the single-claim (len(claims) != 1) check. In compare_rpc: the eth_getLogs length check, so a live response with an extra log still matches. I re-probed eight of the builder's 15 listed mutants, and all eight are killed as claimed.
